title: Subject and object questions: Who called you?

objective.en: Ask about the subject without do, does or did (Who called you?) and about the object with them (Who did you call?).
objective.fr: Poser des questions sur le sujet sans do, does ni did (Who called you?) et sur l'objet avec eux (Who did you call?).
objective.de: Fragen zum Subjekt ohne do, does oder did stellen (Who called you?) und zum Objekt mit ihnen (Who did you call?).

label.fr: Questions sur le sujet : Who called you?

instructions.en: Read the explanation and the examples.
instructions.de: Lies die Erklärung und die Beispiele.

text.en:
In a **subject question** the question word is the subject, so you do not use `do`, `does` or `did`. Put the verb straight after the question word: `Who called you?` `What happened?`

The verb keeps its normal form: **-s** in the present and the past form in the past.

- `Who lives here?` (not `Who does live here?`)
- `What made that noise?` (not `What did make that noise?`)
- `Which team won?`
text.fr:
Dans une **question sur le sujet**, le mot interrogatif est le sujet : on n'emploie donc pas `do`, `does` ni `did`. Le verbe suit directement le mot interrogatif : `Who called you?` `What happened?`

Le verbe garde sa forme normale : **-s** au présent et la forme du passé au prétérit.

- `Who lives here?` (et non `Who does live here?`)
- `What made that noise?` (et non `What did make that noise?`)
- `Which team won?`
text.de:
In einer **Subjektfrage** ist das Fragewort das Subjekt, deshalb benutzt man kein `do`, `does` oder `did`. Das Verb steht direkt hinter dem Fragewort: `Who called you?` `What happened?`

Das Verb behält seine normale Form: **-s** im Präsens und die Vergangenheitsform im Past Simple.

- `Who lives here?` (nicht `Who does live here?`)
- `What made that noise?` (nicht `What did make that noise?`)
- `Which team won?`

label.en: Object questions: Who did you call?
label.fr: Questions sur l'objet : Who did you call?

instructions.en: Read the explanation and the examples.
instructions.de: Lies die Erklärung und die Beispiele.

text.en:
In an **object question** the question word is the object, so you need an auxiliary: `do`, `does` or `did`, then the subject, then the base verb: `Who did you call?` `What did she say?`

Compare the two patterns:

- Subject question: `Who called Tom?` (Who = the person who called)
- Object question: `Who did Tom call?` (Who = the person Tom called)

Ask yourself: is the question word doing the action (subject) or receiving it (object)? With other auxiliaries the order is the same: `What has she bought?`
text.fr:
Dans une **question sur l'objet**, le mot interrogatif est le complément : il faut donc un auxiliaire, `do`, `does` ou `did`, puis le sujet, puis le verbe à l'infinitif sans to : `Who did you call?` `What did she say?`

Comparez les deux structures :

- Question sur le sujet : `Who called Tom?` (Who = la personne qui a appelé)
- Question sur l'objet : `Who did Tom call?` (Who = la personne que Tom a appelée)

Demandez-vous : le mot interrogatif fait-il l'action (sujet) ou la reçoit-il (objet) ? Avec les autres auxiliaires, l'ordre est le même : `What has she bought?`
text.de:
In einer **Objektfrage** ist das Fragewort das Objekt, deshalb braucht man ein Hilfsverb: `do`, `does` oder `did`, dann das Subjekt und dann das Verb in der Grundform: `Who did you call?` `What did she say?`

Vergleiche die beiden Muster:

- Subjektfrage: `Who called Tom?` (Who = die Person, die angerufen hat)
- Objektfrage: `Who did Tom call?` (Who = die Person, die Tom angerufen hat)

Frag dich: Führt das Fragewort die Handlung aus (Subjekt) oder erfährt es sie (Objekt)? Bei anderen Hilfsverben ist die Reihenfolge gleich: `What has she bought?`
